central_reading: The three Siddhitrayī texts (APS, Sambandhasiddhi, Īśvarasiddhi) have now all been translated. None supplies the missing nondual universalization proof. APS asserts but does not prove it. Sambandhasiddhi assumes the framework. Īśvarasiddhi is intentionally dualistic. The decombination bind remains: Pratyabhijñā has not specified how unrestricted manifestation produces private exclusion profiles.

argument_edges.rationale: APS 17 claims universal synthesis but Abhinavagupta limits anusandhāna per body.
Sambandhasiddhi assumes rather than proves the Pratyabhijñā ontology.
Īśvarasiddhi explicitly leaves nondual proof to another text.
The limitation mechanism has not been specified; the trilemma shows why this matters.
The missing Lᵢ is exactly Pratyabhijñā's version of the missing Λ.

state_of_play_delta.cand:siva-decombination: Pressured by the accumulated evidence from all three Siddhis: APS asserts but doesn't prove, Sambandhasiddhi assumes the framework, Īśvarasiddhi is dualistic. Plus the formal trilemma on Lᵢ.
state_of_play_delta.current_best_answer: The three Siddhitrayī texts do not contain the missing nondual proof. The decombination bind — why unrestricted manifestation produces private exclusion profiles — remains unsolved within the Pratyabhijñā tradition.
